trickyParts: Oh My Pi's state root follows the data root's rule exactly (`state: XDG_STATE_HOME-candidate ?? configRoot` in its DirResolver, the same existsSync test and agent-dir gate), confirmed on the pinned 18.6.0 by where `omp models list` writes its log: `omp config get` writes none and proves nothing.

A push that lands within seconds of main moving gets no `pull_request` run: GitHub computes the merge ref against the new main first, finds the head conflicting, and starts nothing; the next forward merge starts the runs.

`skills/legion-worker/SKILL.md` has a 500-line guard (`packages/pi-legion/src/skills-guard.test.ts`); two branches each adding a few lines to it merge over the guard with no textual conflict, and the merge is where the rewrap happens.

In the shim's `podSafeEnvironment`, EnsureStateHome runs after `podsafety.Apply`, on the environment Oh My Pi will start with, and uses the shim's working directory as Oh My Pi's for the StateRoot assertion (the launcher runs the shim in the pod's WorkingDir, which the child inherits).

Oh My Pi's state root is `$XDG_STATE_HOME/omp/profiles/<profile>` only when that directory already exists at start (its compiled resolver, `/opt/omp/bin/omp` in this pod); otherwise the config root; and the lookup is skipped when PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR names a directory other than the profile's own `agent` dir (a pod names exactly that). Sessions are data-class and stay on the issue volume; `run/daemons`, `logs`, `browser-profiles`, `terminal-sessions` are state-class and move with the state home.

The role's agent environment travels in the launcher start command's Env (`launchEnvironment` → `launcherCommand`), not the container's `Env` (which carries only the kubelet-resolved entries), so a per-role value set in `mainEnvironment` reaches each role's shim without touching the pod template or the goldens.

Under tmux the second role of one issue finds the first's `broker.sock` on the shared filesystem and shares its broker as designed; the fault is the pod's alone, where the network namespace is shared and the filesystems are not.

main's `RoleResources.Reserved()` (the `resource-limits` capability) over this branch's two-field shape is always true after load, so the capability row is `present` on every Kubernetes deployment and main's `--check-config` test cases that expected it open had to move to the reservation semantics.

A process-tree RSS sampler over `ps -eo pid,ppid,rss` every 0.5 s stands in for `/usr/bin/time -v`, which the image lacks; summed RSS double-counts shared pages (a headless Chromium's 11 processes summed to 4.2 GiB with a 450 MiB largest process), so the largest-process figure is reported beside it.
api.State's Issue view carries no tree: an issue's tree is recorded on its claims (OperatorClaim.tree, `legion claims list --json`), which is where a proof reads it

The sweep's delete fence: since ensureSandbox relabels a suspended Sandbox in place (same UID), only {UID, ResourceVersion} tells a re-admitted issue's Sandbox from the orphan the informer snapshot saw
A gone-wait in bash: `[ -z "$(cmd)" ]` discards cmd's status; `out=$(cmd) && [ -z "$out" ]` is what every such wait uses
The production floor is memory-bound (instance-memory Gt 65535), so the smallest allowed type is an 8-vCPU/64 GiB node and a 3 CPU / 12 GiB pod fits two per node, cpu binding
gVisor exposes no cgroup files: the in-pod checks are nproc == max(2, ceil(sum cpu limits)) and MemTotal within 3% of the summed memory limits — confirmed live by stage 4a `resources`
